title: Modal Verbs: Possibility & Deduction

vocab.ex: Might expresses possibility.
Must can express logical deduction.
Must be means you are almost sure.
Can't be expresses that something is impossible.
Might and could soften an opinion.
That's just a guess, I'm not sure.
Based on the evidence, he must be lying.
I'm not sure; it could be true.
She might be at home right now.
It could be true, I'm not sure.
The meeting may be cancelled.
He must be tired after that trip.
That can't be right, check again.
The road was wet, it must have rained.
He can't have finished already, it's too soon.
She might have forgotten about the meeting.
He must be stuck in traffic.
She might be on vacation this week.
They must have run out of time.
He might have forgotten the appointment.
It's late, she must be asleep.
He can't answer, he might have lost his phone.
Based on the evidence, she must be right.
The wet umbrella is a clue that it rained.
That explanation must be true, it makes sense.
It's unlikely to rain today, but it might.
She's probably at work now.
That can't be true, definitely not.
You should double-check before you decide.
Don't jump to conclusions, it might be a mistake.

expressions.meaning: Pode ser dos dois jeitos / não dá pra saber
expressions.example: The match could go either way.
The door is locked, that must be it.
I wouldn't be surprised if she was late again.
Why is the light on? Beats me.

sentences: She might be at home right now.
It could be true, I'm not sure.
He must be tired after that long trip.
That can't be right, let's check again.
The road is wet, it must have rained.
She might have forgotten about the meeting.
He's not answering, he might have lost his phone.
Don't jump to conclusions, it could be a mistake.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs: Possibilidade e Dedução
rules: Might e could expressam possibilidade: It might rain later. (talvez chova)
Must be expressa uma dedução lógica forte, quase certeza: The lights are off, they must be out.
Can't be expressa que algo é logicamente impossível: He can't be at work, I just saw him at home.
Para o passado, use modal + have + particípio: must have been, might have been, can't have been.

quiz.q: The lights are off, they ___ be out.
It ___ rain later, take an umbrella just in case.
He answered in French, he ___ be from Quebec.
That ___ be right, I just spoke to her yesterday.
The ground is wet, it ___ have rained last night.

Don't jump to conclusions, it could be a mistake.
